content.comment_body: Hello, how can I update the value through the display in a message text while the SD card is in the [product_name]? After turning the power off and on again, the [product_name] loads the previous value from the SD card.
After modifying the value, you need to save the program from the [product_name] to the SD card. This is the only way to retain changes.
That's exactly the issue. With each restart, the [product_name] reads the program from the mSD card.
However, to do this, you must set the [product_name] to STOP mode. It's not possible while it is in operator mode.
When I insert an mSD card into my [product_name] [version_no] and copy the program to the card, any value changes are stored on it. Is your mSD card write-protected or copy-protected?
Sorry, it's actually [article_no].standard. The SD card isn't protected.
With [product_name] [article_no].Standard, this feature isn't possible. Please refer to the previous posts.
I write programs in LAD. Does that matter?

No. The ability to change parameters in a message text stored on a program on an mSD card is available in later versions. [product_name] [version_no]? FS05 or FS06? Not sure. However, it's unrelated to the programming language.
Is the solution simply not to use an SD card in the [product_name]? Thank you all for your help.

In your case, you don't need to save the program to the mSD card, or you can copy it after changing a parameter if it's allowed. After reviewing older [document]s, this feature is available on [product_name][version_no].FS5 or newer.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want to update values via display on the [product_name] while an SD card is present. Current behavior reverts values to defaults after a power cycle, since the module reloads the program from the SD card. Several users confirm that the hardware does not support persistent operator changes unless manually saved to the SD card, which requires entering STOP mode and cannot be done while running. The standard version ([article_no]) lacks support for retaining operator-made changes between restarts, highlighting a limitation in dynamic data persistence.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that changes made via display in operator mode will be kept after a power cycle, without needing to manually save or stop the device.
